sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from one fixed strictly positive compatible observed law \(p\).
sampling_model.treatment: The macro intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=c_x)\) is the causal query and is not randomly assigned in the observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is positive; regular-stratum inference imposes the fixed margin \(\min_a p(a)\ge\eta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is required: \(\widehat p_N\) is the empirical complete-cell law, circuit derivatives are obtained by arithmetic-DAG differentiation on \(\mathcal U\), the plug-in estimator uses a fixed uniform target vector and zero covariance outside \(\mathcal U\), and boundary inference propagates \(R_N\) through every certified guard.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 6 states that the ID algorithm is sound and complete for macro effects in an acyclic C-DAG.
Theorem 4 states that failure of one cluster do-calculus rule has a compatible ADMG witness under its cluster-size condition.
The ID algorithm returns an observational expression or a hedge and is complete for one fixed recursive semi-Markovian graph.
Equivalent single conditional-interventional kernels in one ADMG admit a canonical derivation using at most four do-calculus rule applications.
Theorem 2 gives a sufficient graphical criterion for one causal effect to share an identifying formula across candidate SA-MPDAGs.
For functional causal structures with two binary observed variables, algebraic elimination yields feasibility tests and can recover identifiable causal parameters.
Algorithm IDP identifies effects uniformly over one PAG-represented Markov equivalence class whenever its recursive criterion succeeds.
The public manuscript claims that three representatives per cluster preserve macro identifiability and that the resulting procedure is atomically complete.

tldr: A known arbitrary clustering of an acyclic micro causal system can create a cyclic macro diagram and a union of observational model images. The proposal characterizes uniform macro-effect identification by local ID plus agreement on every common-law overlap, then asks for a constructive ranked saturation required to preserve guard coverage, local values, and all pairwise comparison cells until it emits one common-value guarded circuit or two bounded positive finite SCMs with the same complete observed law and different macro effects. An affirmative construction yields Global-CID and, conditionally on its size analysis, the displayed elementary bound; total branchwise multinomial inference uses a harmless fallback outside its local extension neighborhood, while a simultaneous region remains valid at guard boundaries.

project_justification.gap: Published C-DAG completeness covers acyclic cluster diagrams, and recent cyclic C-DMG results prove soundness or rulewise completeness but explicitly do not reconcile different derivations across compatible refinements or furnish a complete common-law collision converse.
project_justification.niche: Finite alphabets and known memberships make the arbitrary-cluster model a finite union of recursive ADMG images, so the unresolved mathematical object is an overlap-sensitive symbolic normal form rather than another local do-calculus rule.
project_justification.fill: Global-CID combines ordinary ID within each exact refinement with a ranked fixing-overlap saturation satisfying explicit coverage and value-preservation invariants, emitting either one common-value guarded functional valid on the entire union or a bounded pair of legal positive SCMs that certifies failure. Its elementary bound is conditional on constructing and sizing that saturation, and its circuit feeds a total regular-stratum estimator and boundary-robust inference.

related_work: ShpitserPearl2006JointID, Theorems 4, 6, and 7, establishes the formula-or-hedge standard for one fixed ADMG and supplies the local recursive engine. AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG, Theorems 5 and 6, lifts do-calculus and ID to acyclic cluster diagrams but excludes cyclic quotients. FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG, Theorem 4 and its conclusion, treats cyclic cluster quotients but explicitly limits completeness to individual rule failures and leaves different successful rule sequences and a complete nonidentification criterion unresolved. TehSadeghiSoo2025RobustID, Theorem 2, motivates robustness across non-equivalent graph candidates but provides a sufficient common-expression criterion on SA-MPDAGs rather than an overlap-sensitive if-and-only-if result. JaberZhangBareinboim2019PAGID handles a single PAG equivalence class whose members share one statistical model, unlike the union of refinement-specific observable images here. TikkaHelskeKarvanen2023TransitClusters proves preservation for a restricted contraction class and demonstrates why arbitrary clustering is not benign. LeeSpekkens2017AlgebraicCausal shows that semialgebraic elimination can characterize tiny finite functional structures; it is used only as a certificate checker, not as the identification algorithm. YvernesEtAl2026DerivationGraphs gives a four-step normal form for individual interventional kernels in one ADMG and identifies finite normal forms for complete ID expressions as open. ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF supplies fixed-graph finite canonical SCMs, while the proposed bounded collision theorem adds paired exact-refinement activity, positivity, and complete-law equality. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022Semiparametric and FangSantos2019DirectionalInference inform the smooth-branch and nonregular-boundary inference layers after graphical identification is settled.
technical_internal_limitation: The ordinary finite-union equivalence is semantic and does not itself provide a guarded circuit. Raw rational comparison is unsound because two formulas may differ on the free simplex yet agree on the intersection of their refinement images. Conversely, separately constructed hedge witnesses need not share one observed law, and the union of acyclic witness refinements may contain a directed cycle. The ranked fixing-overlap normal form must preserve its guard-cover, local-value, exact-unresolved-pair, and no-lost-disagreement invariant until it produces the fully encoded positive or negative terminal certificate. Generic real quantifier elimination may check a terminal algebraic certificate but does not count as Global-CID, and the \(E_4\) bound is not asserted without the missing decreasing-rank construction and size analysis.
honest_scope: The semantic gluing criterion, finite refinement enumeration, bounded-support compression architecture, and multinomial inference reductions have direct proof routes. The constructive overlap normal form remains open: its saturation invariant and terminal encodings are specified, but a decreasing rank, branch coverage proof, exact witness extraction, and size analysis must still be supplied. The \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\) complexity and output bound is conditional on that construction. The result concerns complete macro interventions on known clusters in finite recursive semi-Markovian SCMs with exact graph activity and positive observed laws; it does not identify micro interventions, cyclic micro-SCM effects, or clinical efficacy. On acyclic C-DAGs and singleton partitions it must reduce to the published cluster-ID and ordinary-ID results.

definitions.name: Compatible micro-refinement class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R(H)=\{G\in\mathsf{DMG}(V):G\text{ has acyclic directed part and }\operatorname{clust}_{C}(G)=H\}\).

definitions.name: Compatible positive finite SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M(H,d)=\{M\in\mathsf{RSM}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V):G_M\in\mathfrak R(H),\ |\operatorname{dom}_M(v)|=d(v)\text{ for every }v\in V,\text{ and }P_M(a)>0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: Global uniform identification
definitions.construction: The target is uniformly identified when there exists \(f:\Omega_H\to\Delta(\mathcal A_Y)^{\mathcal A_X}\) such that \(f(P_M)(c_y;c_x)=Q_M(c_y;c_x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) and every \((c_x,c_y)\).

definitions.name: Refinement-local ID functional
definitions.construction: For \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\), run ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}(G,X,Y)\); on success, store its shared rational arithmetic DAG as \(\phi_G\), with every denominator accompanied by its positive-law guard.

definitions.name: Guarded arithmetic circuit
definitions.construction: A circuit is a finite list \(F=((g_b,F_b))_{b=1}^m\) in which each \(g_b\) is a guard, each \(F_b\) is an arithmetic DAG over rational constants and cells \(p(a)\) using \(+,-,\times,/\) and finite sums, the guards cover \(\Omega_H\), every divisor is strictly positive on its branch domain, and \(F_b(p)=F_{b'}(p)\) whenever \(p\in\Omega_H\) satisfies both \(g_b\) and \(g_{b'}\). For \(p\in\Omega_H\), \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\) is this common value for any satisfied guard, so evaluation is total and independent of branch choice even when guards overlap.

definitions.name: Adjacent-singleton cyclic quotient and exact refinements
definitions.construction: Take \(V_{\star}=\{a,b,c,d\}\), binary alphabets, and \(C_{\star}=\{K_a,K_b,K_{cd}\}\) with \(K_a=\{a\}\), \(K_b=\{b\}\), and \(K_{cd}=\{c,d\}\). Let \(H_{\star}\) have exactly the directed edges \(K_a\to K_b\), \(K_a\to K_{cd}\), \(K_{cd}\to K_a\), \(K_b\to K_{cd}\), and \(K_{cd}\to K_b\), and no bidirected edges. Set \(G_{1\star}=\{c\to a,c\to b,a\to b,a\to d,b\to d\}\) with order \(c,a,b,d\), and \(G_{2\star}=\{d\to a,d\to b,a\to b,a\to c,b\to c\}\) with order \(d,a,b,c\). Finally set \(EX_{\star}=\{K_a\}\) and \(EY_{\star}=\{K_b\}\).

definitions.name: Common strictly positive law
definitions.construction: Define \(p_{\star}\) through the \(G_{1\star}\)-factorization by \(p_{\star}(c=1)=1/2\), \(p_{\star}(a=1\mid c=0)=1/4\), \(p_{\star}(a=1\mid c=1)=3/4\), \([p_{\star}(b=1\mid a,c)]_{(a,c)}=((1/8,3/8),(5/8,7/8))\), and \([p_{\star}(d=1\mid a,b)]_{(a,b)}=((1/5,2/5),(3/5,4/5))\), using complements for value zero and row-major order for binary parent tuples. Equivalently, the same law has the \(G_{2\star}\)-factorization \(p_{\star}(d=1)=1/2\), \([p_{\star}(a=1\mid d)]_{d=0,1}=(19/80,61/80)\), \([p_{\star}(b=1\mid a,d)]_{(a,d)}=((9/61,6/19),(13/19,52/61))\), and \([p_{\star}(c=1\mid a,b)]_{(a,b)}=((5/26,1/2),(1/2,21/26))\).

definitions.name: Exact-active finite SCM realizations of the common law
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), construct \(M_{j\star}\) in the displayed topological order of \(G_{j\star}\) by assigning one independent finite uniform exogenous variable to each observed vertex and using the inverse-CDF response table from the corresponding conditional probability in \(p_{\star}\). For \(M_{1\star}\), use uniform support sizes \(2,4,8,5\) for the response tables of \(c,a,b,d\). For \(M_{2\star}\), use uniform support sizes \(2,80,1159,26\) for the response tables of \(d,a,b,c\). Set a binary child to one exactly on the initial segment whose size equals its displayed success probability times the relevant support size.

definitions.name: Candidate bounded common-law collision certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Certificate}=(G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) with \(G_j\in\mathfrak R(H)\), \(M_j\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\), \(G_{M_j}=G_j\), \(P_{M_1}=P_{M_2}=p\), \(Q_{M_1}(c_y;c_x)\neq Q_{M_2}(c_y;c_x)\), and every latent root of either model having support at most \(B(H,d)\); rational or real-algebraic table entries are encoded by integer polynomials and isolating intervals.

definitions.name: Paired response-table compression handle
definitions.construction: Start from any same-law pair witnessing failure of uniform identification. Replace each finite latent root by its deterministic response-type representation, couple the two observed-law moment systems through their common cell vector, and apply support reduction to the joint vector of observational cells, all macro intervention cells, active-edge contrasts, and normalization coordinates. The target is a pair that preserves the complete common observed law, every macro intervention distribution, strict positivity, prescribed observed alphabets, and both exact active micrographs while bounding each retained latent-root support by \(B(H,d)\).

definitions.name: Ranked fixing-overlap saturation handle
definitions.construction: Starting from \((G,\phi_G,\Omega_G)_{G\in\mathfrak R(H)}\), design a finite worklist saturation using \(\mathsf{Ops}\). Every reachable overlap state must satisfy the following invariant: its guards form a finite cover of every feasible pair \((G,p)\) retained from the initial family; on each guarded piece, every stored fixing kernel and arithmetic DAG equals the corresponding \(\phi_G(p)\) on \(\Omega_G\); each unresolved refinement pair records precisely the common-law cells not yet certified equal or separated; and every transition preserves covered feasible pairs and cannot discard a cell on which two retained target values disagree. A terminal positive state is encoded as the finite list \(((g_b,F_b))_{b=1}^m\), with guard coverage, positive-divisor annotations, and pairwise common-value identities sufficient for \(\operatorname{Eval}\). A terminal negative state is encoded as \((G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) together with topological-order, exact-coarsening, response-table, latent-support, positivity, complete-law-equality, and target-separation checks, using integer-polynomial and isolating-interval encodings for real-algebraic entries. Derive a well-founded rank that strictly decreases after every nonterminal transition.

definitions.name: Global-CID
definitions.construction: Given a certified paired response-table compressor satisfying the collision-compression handle and a certified terminating saturation satisfying the ranked fixing-overlap handle, enumerate \(\mathfrak R(H)\) and run ordinary ID on every refinement. If a local run fails, apply the supplied compressor to its hedge witness. Otherwise apply the supplied saturation to the local formulas. Return the resulting common guarded circuit or cross-refinement collision certificate after exact checks of graph compatibility, positivity, full observed-law equality, branch coverage, overlap common-value identities, denominator safety, latent support, and target separation.

definitions.name: Empirical-multinomial branch plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: On \(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U\), set \(\widehat Q_N=\widetilde F_S(\widehat p_N)\) and use the Jacobian plug-in covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_F\); outside \(\mathcal U\), set \(\widehat Q_N(c_y;c_x)=1/|\mathcal A_Y|\) for every \((c_x,c_y)\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_F=0\). In both cases define \(\mathcal W_N\) from these total objects. At the population law, the influence vector is \(\psi_p(a)=J_F(p)(e_a-p)\) and the covariance is \(\Sigma_F(p)\).

definitions.name: Guard-propagated simultaneous target region
definitions.construction: Construct \(R_N\) with radius \(\varepsilon_N\), then propagate every point of \(R_N\) through every circuit branch whose guard and denominator conditions it satisfies, and take the closure of the union to obtain \(\mathcal I_N(F)\).

statements.statement: The compatible refinement class is finite and can be enumerated from the labelled input, with \(|\mathfrak R(H)|\le 2^{3n(n-1)/2}\); every enumerated graph carries a topological ordering certificate for its directed part and an exact coarsening certificate.
statements.justification: Finiteness turns arbitrary clustering into a finite union problem without confusing a cyclic quotient with a cyclic micrograph.
statements.gap: AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG assumes an acyclic cluster graph, while FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG allows cyclic quotients but does not enumerate exact known-size refinements for global identification.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite input family for the Global-CID search and its explicit complexity accounting.

statements.statement: The macro target is uniformly identified over \(\mathfrak M(H,d)\) if and only if both conditions hold: it is identified within every \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\), and for every \(G_1,G_2\in\mathfrak R(H)\) the corresponding local target maps agree at every \(p\in\Omega_{G_1}\cap\Omega_{G_2}\). When the conditions hold, the map \(f(p)=\phi_G(p)\) for any \(G\) with \(p\in\Omega_G\) is well defined on \(\Omega_H\).
statements.justification: This preliminary gluing fact isolates the semantic overlap obligation without claiming to solve its constructive representation problem.
statements.gap: TehSadeghiSoo2025RobustID gives a sufficient shared-expression criterion for candidate SA-MPDAGs; it does not characterize agreement only on common observable-law images of hidden-variable refinements.
statements.consumer: It supplies the correctness specification against which the ranked overlap saturation is judged.

statements.statement: Does every failure of uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,d)\) admit a collision certificate in which every latent root has at most \(B(H,d)=2^n\prod_{v\in V}d(v)+4n^2+1\) states, while preserving the complete common observed law, all macro intervention distributions, strict observed positivity, prescribed alphabets, and both exact active micrographs? The Handle is the paired response-table compression that retains the joint observational, interventional, activity, and normalization coordinates before support reduction.
statements.justification: A general formula-or-collision theorem needs a finite inspectable witness theorem beyond the single explicit cyclic example.
statements.gap: ShpitserPearl2006JointID constructs a hedge pair for one fixed ADMG, and ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF canonicalizes one fixed graph; neither jointly enforces a same-positive-law collision across two exact refinements with active advertised edges.
statements.consumer: A positive solution supplies the bounded negative-output subroutine required by the conditional Global-CID theorem.

statements.statement: For the binary input \(V_{\star}=\{a,b,c,d\}\), \(C_{\star}=\{K_a,K_b,K_{cd}\}\), \(H_{\star}\), \(EX_{\star}=\{K_a\}\), and \(EY_{\star}=\{K_b\}\) in the explicit construction, \(G_{1\star}\) and \(G_{2\star}\) are acyclic exact refinements of \(H_{\star}\). Their common skeleton is \(K_4\) without \(c-d\), neither graph has an unshielded collider, and their common positive observational model is characterized by \(c\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}d\mid(a,b)\). The displayed law \(p_{\star}\) is strictly positive and factorizes over both graphs. The inverse-CDF models \(M_{1\star}\) and \(M_{2\star}\) have exact active graphs \(G_{1\star}\) and \(G_{2\star}\), respectively, and both induce \(p_{\star}\). Nevertheless, \(\Pr_{M_{1\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=0))=1/4\) whereas \(\Pr_{M_{2\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=0))=537/2318\), and \(\Pr_{M_{1\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=1))=3/4\) whereas \(\Pr_{M_{2\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=1))=1781/2318\); the differences are \(85/4636\) and \(-85/4636\). Every refinement of \(H_{\star}\) is a DAG and hence is locally identified, but the macro effect is not uniformly identified. This is vertex-minimal among feasible directed cycles containing two adjacent singleton clusters: a cycle consisting only of singleton clusters would force a directed micro-cycle, so three clusters and one additional vertex are necessary, and sizes \((1,1,2)\) attain the bound. Consequently, any terminating saturation satisfying the ranked overlap handle and its exact equality-or-separation invariant must detect or reproduce a valid separating certificate for this input.
statements.justification: The explicit arithmetic collision establishes a strict, independently checkable failure of refinement-by-refinement identification in the smallest adjacent-singleton cyclic regime.
statements.gap: AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG excludes cyclic cluster graphs, while FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG does not decide common-law disagreement between individually identified exact refinements.
statements.consumer: It gives the cyclic lisinopril--stroke grouping a concrete warning pattern and supplies a regression test that every candidate overlap saturation must pass.

statements.statement: Can one construct the ranked fixing-overlap saturation specified by the handle using only \(\mathsf{Ops}\), with every reachable state satisfying its guard-cover, local-value preservation, exact unresolved-pair, and no-lost-disagreement invariant, and with every terminal state encoded either as a guarded circuit whose overlapping satisfied branches have one common \(\operatorname{Eval}\) value or as the fully checked tuple \((G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) of a bounded collision certificate? The construction must terminate and return the circuit exactly when \(\phi_{G_1}=\phi_{G_2}\) on every nonempty \(\Omega_{G_1}\cap\Omega_{G_2}\). A further quantitative objective is to make its state count, bit complexity, and encoded terminal output at most \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\); this \(E_4\) bound is conditional on supplying such a decreasing-rank construction and size analysis.
statements.justification: This constructive normal form is the sole non-routine bridge from semantic finite-union identification to a graph-native algorithm.
statements.gap: YvernesEtAl2026DerivationGraphs gives a four-step normal form for single conditional-interventional kernels in one ADMG and explicitly leaves finite representations for full ID expressions open; LeeSpekkens2017AlgebraicCausal supplies general elimination only for tiny finite functional structures.
statements.consumer: Solving it supplies the terminating compilation or separating-pair step required by Global-CID without relabelling unrestricted real quantifier elimination as causal identification.

statements.statement: Given a terminating saturation system satisfying the ranked fixing-overlap handle, Global-CID terminates on every feasible encoded input and returns exactly one of two checkable objects. A formula return is a guarded circuit \(F\) whose overlap common-value condition makes \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)\) total and satisfies \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)(c_y;c_x)=Q_M(c_y;c_x)\) simultaneously for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) and every \((c_x,c_y)\). A negative return is a bounded collision certificate. The algorithm returns a circuit if and only if the macro target is uniformly identified. If the supplied saturation additionally has state count, transition cost, and terminal encoding length within the quantitative objective of the overlap-normal-form question, then the total bit complexity and encoded output length are at most \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\).
statements.justification: The formula-or-collision dichotomy gives arbitrary clustering the same constructive identification standard that ordinary ID provides for one known ADMG.
statements.gap: AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG proves ID completeness only for acyclic cluster diagrams, and FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG Theorem 4 is rulewise completeness that its conclusion says does not compare different rule sequences or prove a complete nonidentification characterization.
statements.consumer: Anand and Hripcsak's ALARM grouping can receive either one implementable effect functional or two explicit micro-level mechanisms showing why the chosen clinical clustering is insufficient.

statements.statement: On the acyclic C-DAG domain of AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG, Global-CID returns a circuit if and only if cluster ID succeeds and its circuit agrees with the published cluster-ID functional on every positive compatible law. On singleton partitions it reduces to ShpitserPearl2006JointID. The inclusion is strict: there exists a feasible known-size cyclic quotient with acyclic refinements for which every refinement is locally identified but refinement-specific effects disagree at one common strictly positive observed law; Global-CID returns the separating pair, whereas rulewise completeness alone does not decide this global clash. Hence the result strictly strengthens the published acyclic C-DAG theorem and the rulewise cyclic C-DMG criterion on their common recursive-SCM target.
statements.justification: The required sanity reductions and a strict cyclic separation prevent the result from being merely an analogue on a self-defined class.
statements.gap: Neither AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG nor FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG handles the common-law disagreement of individually identified exact refinements.
statements.consumer: The cyclic lisinopril--stroke grouping receives a definitive answer without pretending that the cyclic macro quotient is itself a recursive micrograph.

statements.statement: For a circuit return and a fixed stratum \(S\), \(\Pr_p(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U)\to1\). On the event \(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U\), the total definitions coincide with \(\widehat Q_N=\widetilde F_S(\widehat p_N)\) and the Jacobian plug-in covariance. Consequently, without conditioning, \(\sqrt N\{\widehat Q_N-\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\}\) converges to \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_F(p))\), with influence vector \(\psi_p(O_i)=J_F(p)(e_{O_i}-p)\); \(\widehat\Sigma_F\) is consistent, its rank equals \(r\) with probability tending to one, and \(\mathcal W_N\) has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) within the range of \(\Sigma_F(p)\).
statements.justification: A graphically identified circuit becomes empirically useful only after its branchwise sampling law and covariance are explicit.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022Semiparametric derives influence estimators for one fixed graphical functional, not a circuit compiled across observable-model overlaps.
statements.consumer: The ALARM analysis obtains automatic-differentiation standard errors for every reported macro outcome coordinate on a certified regular stratum.

statements.statement: For every \(N\ge1\), every \(p\in\Omega_H\), and every circuit return, \(\Pr_p\{\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\in\mathcal I_N(F)\}\ge1-\alpha\). The guarantee holds without selecting one empirical branch and remains valid at intersections of equality guards; any certified outer approximation to \(\mathcal I_N(F)\) inherits the same coverage.
statements.justification: Guard intersections are statistically nonregular, so honest inference must propagate uncertainty through all near-compatible branches rather than condition on a selected formula.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019DirectionalInference treats directionally differentiable maps, while the present region exploits finite multinomial concentration and certified guard coverage for a union of graphical model images.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain a valid finite-sample target region when empirical ALARM cell frequencies lie near a structural or formula-agreement boundary.
